entries.title: Three fixes: sub-session restore, report session scoping, and Grip track colour sync
entries.summary: Three bugs are resolved: (1) Restoring a deleted parent session from **History → Trash** no longer brings back sub-sessions that were independently deleted — those stay in Trash with their own records. (2) Event reports that filter on session **Status** (for Contacts, Accounts, Exhibitors, or Sponsors) no longer return records from other events. (3) A bulk **Sync to Grip** now sends the updated track colour to every session immediately after the track is changed, without requiring each session to be individually edited first; tag changes are also detected correctly.

where.path: History → Trash; Reporting → Reports; Apps → Grip → Sync

entries.use_case: Organizers who use sub-sessions, cross-event reporting on session status, or the Grip integration will see more accurate data without manual workarounds: deleted sub-sessions stay deleted after a parent restore, saved queries return only the right event's contacts, and a single bulk sync pushes track colour changes to Grip.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that restoring a parent session unexpectedly brought back a sub-session they had deleted, that a saved report query returns contacts or accounts from the wrong event, or that Grip sessions show a stale track colour after a bulk sync.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using sub-sessions with independent deletions, customers with cross-event CRM reports filtered on session status (especially America's Credit Unions, event 7019), and customers using the Grip integration (e.g. Enlit EU, event 274).
internal.staff_path: Event → History → Trash (sub-session restore); Org → Reporting → Reports (scoping fix); Event → Apps → Grip → Sync (track colour fix)
internal.gotchas: The report scoping fix covers Contact→Session, Account→Session, Exhibitor→Session, and Sponsor→Session laterals. The Contact lateral was already fixed in the prior release (SB-10105 / #4584); this PR adds the Account, Exhibitor, and Sponsor twins. Existing saved queries will now return correct (narrower) results — customers who relied on the old cross-event behaviour will see fewer rows.
internal.talk_track: Three quiet but impactful fixes shipped together: deleted sub-sessions now stay deleted when you restore their parent, your session-status reports only show contacts from the event you're looking at, and Grip picks up track colour changes the moment you run a bulk sync.

draft.docs_gap: The delete-or-restore section of the sessions guide should note that restoring a parent session only restores sub-sessions that were deleted as part of that same action — sub-sessions deleted independently remain in Trash.

internal.talk_track: The slot counter on the admin Files tab now counts only speaker-uploaded files, the same way the server and the speaker portal do, so the number shown always reflects how many uploads are left.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that organizer-generated files (title slides, merged copies written by Slides) are excluded from slot file counts and do not count toward the slot maximum.

entries.title: Ask (AI Mode) can read, preview and apply CFP form settings in conversation
entries.summary: The AI assistant (Ask / Team Lead) can now read, dry-run and apply **Program → Submission Forms** settings — open/close dates, open-for-submissions toggle, required questions and form fields — directly from the chat panel. Ask shows a before → after diff with warnings (e.g. opening a form past its deadline, a reminder tied to a conditional deadline) and raises an approval card for every destructive change before writing anything. Changes are written through the same tools and permission checks (**forms:write** scope) as the manual settings page, and Ask reads the form back to confirm the result.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable AI Mode; then open the Ask panel on any event page

where.path: Ask panel → Team Lead conversation

entries.use_case: An organizer setting up a new event can tell Ask "Open the General Submission Form until November 14 and make the Title question required" and Ask will preview the change, surface any warnings, ask for confirmation, and apply it — without the organizer navigating to the form settings page.

cs_action.note: AI Mode (Team Lead agent with settings write scope) must be enabled per customer; confirm the customer has forms:write permission on their event role.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to speed up event setup or mentions they want to configure their CFP form without clicking through multiple settings pages.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using AI Mode / Ask who are in CFP setup or mid-cycle form adjustments.
internal.staff_path: Event → Ask panel → Team Lead
internal.gotchas: Requires forms:write scope on the caller's token; blocked changes (e.g. close date before open date) are refused and explained but not applied. The companion UI PR (sessionboard-web-ui-v2) must also be deployed for the approval card rendering to appear.
internal.talk_track: Tell Ask what you want to change on your submission form — open date, close date, required questions — and it will show you exactly what will change and ask you to confirm before touching anything.

draft.docs_gap: The Team Lead guide should add a section explaining that Ask can read, preview and apply CFP submission-form settings, including the approval-card flow and the cross-field warnings it surfaces.
draft.why_use_it: Ask's Team Lead agent lets you set up and adjust your event by describing what you want in plain language. For CFP forms, you can read the current configuration, see a before-and-after preview of any proposed change, and approve writes — all from the chat panel. Ask enforces the same cross-field rules as the settings page (open-before-close, reminder timing, submission limits) and reads the form back after every write to confirm the result.

entries.title: Team Lead approval card shows before → after values and warnings for settings changes
entries.summary: When the Team Lead agent proposes a settings change, the approval card now displays each affected setting as **~~before~~ → after** so admins can see exactly what will change. Any relevant warnings (for example, "Opening makes the form reachable by anyone with its public link") appear as an amber list above the **Approve / Reject** decision.

where.path: Assistant panel → Team Lead approval card

entries.use_case: When an organizer asks the Team Lead to change a form or event setting, they can review the current value alongside the proposed value before approving, reducing the risk of accidentally accepting a change they did not intend.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer is using or evaluating the Team Lead agent and wants to understand how settings changes are reviewed before they take effect.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with the AI Event Agents feature active who uses the Team Lead to manage event settings.
internal.staff_path: Event → Assistant panel → Team Lead tab → pending approval card
internal.gotchas: Requires companion API and agents PRs to be deployed; the card enhancement is inert without the update_settings tool being live.
internal.talk_track: The approval card now shows you the old value crossed out next to the new one, so you always know what you are agreeing to before you click Approve.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the approval card UI, including how before → after rows and amber warnings appear when the Team Lead proposes a settings change.
draft.why_use_it: The Team Lead agent lets organizers make changes to event settings through a conversational interface. Every proposed change is held for human approval, giving the team full control over what the agent actually does. The before → after display and inline warnings make it straightforward to confirm or reject a change with confidence.

entries.title: Campaign submission status filter shows the event's own statuses
entries.summary: The **Submission status** quick filter on a campaign's Recipients step, the advanced **Session fields → Submission status** row and the filter summary now list the statuses configured for the event — the built-ins plus every custom status, with their colours — instead of a fixed Accepted / Pending / Declined / Withdrawn / Waitlisted list. A custom status can be targeted directly, a built-in status also reaches the custom statuses built on it, and **Withdrawn submissions** is its own switch.

where.path: Send → Campaigns → New campaign → Recipients → Submission status

entries.use_case: Events that rank or stage submissions with custom statuses (Legal Review, Under Review, 1st Choice) can email exactly the submitters or speakers in one of those statuses, and no longer see a Waitlisted option the event does not have.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says the campaign status filter offers statuses they do not use, or cannot pick one of their custom statuses (CES, event 5527 reported both).
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using custom submission statuses under Program Settings → Statuses.
internal.staff_path: Event → Send → Campaigns → New campaign → Recipients → Quick filters → Submission status
internal.gotchas: A built-in status (Pending) also matches submissions in a custom status built on it (In Review) — same rule as the Submissions grid. Withdrawn is a flag, not a status, so it sits under the list as its own switch. A campaign saved with a status the event has since archived shows it ticked and labelled (no longer configured) so it can be cleared.
internal.talk_track: Open Recipients and the Submission status list is your event's own statuses — tick a custom one to email exactly the people in it.

entries.title: Campaigns can target subsession participants by subsession status, merged from the parent session
entries.summary: A **Sessions** campaign's Recipients step gains **Subsession participants**: pick the parent sessions as usual, then email the participants of their subsessions whose **Subsession status** matches — for example every **1st Choice** speaker — with session merge tags resolving to the parent session and a new **Subsession** tag group for the qualifying subsession. One email goes out per recipient per parent session, and a **review table** lets you remove anyone from this send before it goes.

where.path: Send → Campaigns → New campaign (Sessions audience) → Recipients → Subsession participants

entries.use_case: Organizers who rank candidate speakers as subsessions of a parent session (1st Choice, 2nd Choice, …) can invite a whole rank to speak on the parent session in one targeted send, with the invite describing the parent session and a per-person review before sending.

cs_action.note: Built for CES (SB-10296); walk them through it on the Recipients step of a Sessions campaign.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer models speaker candidates as subsessions with custom statuses and asks how to email the first-choice speakers for a session without emailing the subsession itself.
internal.who_should_get_it: Programs that stage candidate speakers as subsessions under a parent session — CES / Informa-style shows and medical programs with alternates.
internal.staff_path: Event → Send → Campaigns → New campaign → Audience: Sessions → Recipients → Subsession participants
internal.gotchas: Lives in the campaign wizard only — the Sessions table's bulk Send Emails modal does not have it yet. Session merge tags mean the parent; use the Subsession tag group for the subsession. Not combined with Bundle session participants onto one email. History shows the parent session per email; the qualifying subsession is not recorded there yet.
internal.talk_track: Pick your parent sessions, flip on Subsession participants, tick 1st Choice, and the wizard lists exactly who gets invited — one email per person per session, written about the parent session, with a remove button on every row.

entries.title: Open Team Lead full screen in the Agent window
entries.summary: **Agent window** in the Ask panel's header opens the same Team Lead conversation at full size: a rail with your **Chats**, **Dashboards** and **Reports** in place of the sidebar, answers set like a document with a line showing what Team Lead checked, record cards that open the session or contact beside the chat, saved reports and dashboards that open as canvases next to the conversation, a suggested follow-up you accept with Tab, and a **Decision needed** card before any change. **Back to sidebar** returns to the page you left with Ask docked.

where.path: Ask → Agent window (event or organization top bar)

entries.use_case: Program teams spend the day asking questions and then opening the page that answers each one. In the Agent window they ask once, read the answer, open the record or report beside it, and approve the follow-up work without leaving the conversation.

cs_action.note: Try a few questions on the customer's own event first so you can show an answer with record cards and a report canvas; the page guide and approvals are the same ones the docked panel already shows.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer who already uses Ask, and anyone comparing us on AI: this is the full-screen, agent-first way to run an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organizer; on by default for every organization and event.
internal.staff_path: Any event or org page → Ask → Agent window in the panel header
internal.gotchas: Past conversations under Chats are read-only (start a new one to continue). Record cards appear only when an answer is about a handful of sessions or people; larger answers stay tables. Report canvases show the first rows of long reports.
internal.talk_track: Click Ask, then Agent window, and Team Lead becomes the whole screen: ask which sessions still need a speaker, open one from the card beside the answer, then ask for the reminder emails and approve them — all in one place. Back to sidebar takes you straight back to where you were.

entries.title: See which submissions have every review in, across plans
entries.summary: An Evaluation Plan 2.0 plan's **Submissions** tab now shows, under each title, how many reviews are in across every plan of the event — co-reviews in another category's plan included — for example **12 of 17 reviews**, with a **Reviews complete** badge once every evaluator has finished. A new **Reviews** filter lists **Reviews complete** or **Still reviewing** submissions, and the export follows it. The numbers match the Score Summary Report's **Reviews complete** and **All reviews in** columns.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → open a plan → Submissions → Reviews filter

entries.use_case: Program committees that send some abstracts to a co-reviewer in another category can see from the primary plan which abstracts are fully reviewed, and work only those, without reconciling two plans by hand.

cs_action.note: IAS-USA asked for this (co-review across category plans); let them know the filter is live on their category plans.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reviews the same abstracts in more than one plan, or asks how to tell when every reviewer is done.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running co-review or multi-category review on Evaluation Plans 2.0: IAS-USA first.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Evaluation → plan → Submissions → Reviews filter
internal.gotchas: Counts every human evaluator in every v2 plan of the event; scouting and public-voting rounds and AI personas are not counted. Abstaining counts as done. A submission with no countable reviews reads Still reviewing.
internal.talk_track: Open the primary category's plan, pick Reviews complete, and you have the abstracts every reviewer, including co-reviewers in other plans, has finished — the same numbers as the Score Summary Report.

entries.title: My Reviews instructions appear in the evaluator's own language
entries.summary: The **My Reviews** instructions card and instructions modal now display the active round's instructions in the evaluator's content language when a translation exists. When no translation is available for that language, a **Shown in [language]** marker appears so evaluators know the text is a fallback. Contact and attendee name fields never show the marker. Contact names (first, last and full name) no longer carry a **Shown in [language]** marker; other untranslated values still do.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Language Variants & Translations; then Event → Evaluations → My Reviews

where.path: Evaluations → My Reviews

entries.use_case: Events with multilingual reviewer panels can now show each evaluator the round instructions in their preferred language, reducing confusion and the need for evaluators to seek out translated guidance elsewhere.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer runs multilingual review panels and wants evaluators to read instructions in their own language.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Language Variants & Translations enabled who have international reviewer pools.
internal.staff_path: Event → Evaluations → My Reviews (sign in as an evaluator whose content language differs from the default)
internal.gotchas: Requires web-api #4683 to be deployed first; against the older API the page degrades safely and shows instructions as before. Person name fields (first name, last name, full_name) never show the fallback marker regardless of translation status.
internal.talk_track: Evaluators now see round instructions in their own language automatically. If a translation is missing, a small marker tells them — and tells you — that the text is a fallback, so you can fill the gap before the review opens.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document that My Reviews instructions respect the evaluator's content language and explain the "Shown in [language]" fallback marker.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's language variants feature lets you maintain translated content — including evaluation round instructions — for each language your reviewers work in. When an evaluator opens My Reviews, they see instructions written for them, not just the default language. A fallback marker makes it clear when a translation has not yet been added, so you know exactly where gaps exist.

entries.title: Ask's AI Mode recognises submissions, files, campaigns, transcripts, media, clips, posters and galleries as clickable record chips

entries.use_case: When an organizer asks Ask a question like "Which abstracts are still pending?" the answer now shows each result as a labelled chip they can click straight into — no need to copy a name and hunt for the record manually. internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer is using AI Mode / Ask and asks why some record types don't appear as clickable chips in answers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with the Agents (AI Event Agents / Coordinators) feature enabled.
internal.staff_path: Ask panel → type a question referencing abstracts, files, campaigns, media, clips, posters or galleries

entries.title: Take action directly from AI Mode record cards with one click
entries.summary: Record cards surfaced in the AI Mode chat now show a **Send reminder** button when a session has unconfirmed speakers or a person is still pending. Clicking the button sends a prompt to Team Lead, which proposes the action and shows an approval card listing the recipients and email subject before anything is sent. where.path: Agent window → chat → record card → Send reminder

entries.use_case: When an organizer asks Team Lead about sessions with unconfirmed speakers, the returned record cards include a Send reminder button so they can trigger participant reminders without leaving the chat — and still review exactly who will receive the email before it goes out.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to chase unconfirmed speakers or pending participants from within the AI Mode chat.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using AI Mode / Team Lead who has sessions with unconfirmed speakers.

entries.title: Swapcard sync places custom-role contacts in their own group, not Speakers

entries.title: Ask sets the correct audience type when drafting an email campaign

entries.title: Advocacy attendee cards now preview, render and embed correctly
entries.summary: Four bugs affecting attendee Advocacy campaigns are resolved. The **Quick Launch** preview now samples real attendees instead of showing a session as the example person. Headshots imported via the attendee CSV importer are downloaded, uploaded to Sessionboard's file store, and drawn on the card. Server-side video renders include the attendee's headshot. The confirmation-page embed and share-crawler OG image no longer show a placeholder card rendered with a stranger's identity — the embed shows no card image until the attendee has generated their own render.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Quick Launch / Confirmation page embed

entries.use_case: Organizers running attendee Advocacy campaigns can now trust that the Quick Launch preview reflects a real attendee, that headshots imported from a CSV actually appear on cards, and that attendees see a blank card slot on the confirmation page rather than a card showing someone else's name and photo.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that the Advocacy preview shows the wrong person, imported headshots are missing from cards, or the confirmation-page embed shows a placeholder card with a stranger's identity.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy with an attendee audience, especially those who import attendees via CSV.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Quick Launch
internal.gotchas: The confirmation-page embed now shows no card image (blank state) until the attendee has opened their share console and a render has been produced. Contacts and group recipients still fall back to the template thumbnail — that is a separate follow-up.
internal.talk_track: These were silent rendering bugs: the preview sampled a session instead of an attendee, imported headshots were blocked by the image proxy, video renders had no headshot, and the embed showed a placeholder card with the editor's sample identity. All four are fixed and ship automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the confirmation-page embed shows no card image until the attendee has generated their own render, and explain the headshot import flow for attendees (external URLs are fetched and re-hosted automatically after import).
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy lets attendees share personalised social cards promoting the event. Each attendee gets a unique link and a card rendered with their own name, headshot and details, so every share looks authentic and drives registrations back to the event.

entries.title: Site image uploads now deliver through the optimised content CDN
entries.summary: Images uploaded to a Site — **Background image**, **Logo**, **Favicon**, **Social share image**, **Portal logo**, and **Image** blocks — are now stored as content-CDN URLs. On the live Site, the CDN automatically resizes and converts them to WebP for each viewport, so hero images and logos load faster without any extra steps.

where.path: Awards → Site → Site settings (or Site builder → Site panel) → Background image / Logo / Favicon / Social share image / Portal logo / Image block

entries.use_case: Any organizer running an Awards Site who uploads a new hero banner or logo will now get automatic responsive resizing and WebP delivery on the live Site, without needing to pre-optimise images before uploading.

cs_action.note: Change is automatic for all new uploads. Existing Sites with Filestack-stored images continue to render correctly; a server-side backfill (web-api#4687) handles previously uploaded images.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why their Site hero image looks large or slow on mobile, or asks about image quality on their Awards Site.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers using Awards Sites who upload images to Site settings or the Site builder.
internal.staff_path: Awards → [Program] → Site → Site settings → Background image / Logo
internal.gotchas: Only newly uploaded images get content-CDN URLs automatically. Sites whose stored hero or logo is still a Filestack URL (cdn.filestackcontent.com/…) will continue to use Filestack delivery until the web-api backfill (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4687) is applied. Image uploaders outside Sites — portal appearance, submission forms, event details, Content Galleries, Poster Gallery, floor maps, org details — are unchanged and still save Filestack URLs.
internal.talk_track: Any new image you upload to your Site settings or Site builder — hero, logo, favicon, social share, or an Image block — is now stored on our content CDN and automatically optimised for each screen size, including WebP on mobile.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that Site image uploads are stored as content-CDN URLs and are automatically resized and converted to WebP for each viewport on the live Site.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Sites serve your landing page, portal, and program pages to attendees and submitters across every device. Images stored through the content CDN are automatically resized for each viewport and converted to modern formats like WebP, so your Site loads quickly on mobile without manual image preparation. The same CDN powers hero banners, logos, favicons, social share images, and Image blocks throughout the builder.

entries.title: Open Ask full-screen in the Agent window, then return to the sidebar
entries.summary: The **Ask** panel header now shows an **Agent window** button that expands the current conversation to a full-screen view at the event or organization level. From the Agent window, clicking **Back to sidebar** returns to the page you came from and re-docks Ask with the same thread intact. The Agent window is now generally available — no Early Access switch required.

where.path: Ask panel → Agent window (header button)

entries.use_case: Organizers who want more screen space while working through a complex question with Ask can expand the conversation full-screen without losing their thread, then jump straight back to the page they were on when they are done.

cs_action.note: The Early Access AI Mode switch has been removed; the Agent window is now on by default for all users. No action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about the AI assistant or mentions wanting more space to work with Ask.
internal.who_should_get_it: All organizers — no gating.
internal.staff_path: Ask panel header → Agent window
internal.gotchas: The old 'AI Mode' Early Access toggle is gone; customers who had it enabled via Early Access will no longer see a switch — the Agent window button replaces it entirely.
internal.talk_track: Click Agent window in the Ask panel header to go full-screen with your current thread. When you're done, hit Back to sidebar and you'll land right back where you were with the conversation still open.

draft.docs_gap: The article should document the new Agent window button in the Ask panel header and the Back to sidebar navigation, replacing any references to the old AI Mode Early Access switch.

Use it when a question needs more back-and-forth than a quick lookup, then return to your previous page with the thread still open in the sidebar.

entries.title: Author and publish native e-sign contract templates in the UI
entries.summary: A **Templates** tab is now available alongside **CRM → Contracts**, giving organizers a full in-browser workflow to create, edit, and publish native Sessionboard e-sign templates without API access. The document editor supports merge variables (contact, session, event fields), ordered signer roles, insertable field blocks (**Signature**, **Initials**, **Date Signed**, **Text**, **Checkbox**), conditional sections, `.docx` import, **Preview as…** a real contact or group, inline publish-problem linting, and revision history with restore. Templates move through **Draft → Published vN → unpublished changes → Archived** states; published templates appear immediately in the **Add Contract → Send with Sessionboard** picker.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Contracts

where.path: CRM → Contracts → Templates

entries.use_case: Organizers who need speakers or sponsors to sign a custom agreement can now draft the template themselves — adding merge fields, signer roles, and conditional clauses — and publish it directly from the Contracts tab, without involving a developer or Docusign account.

cs_action.note: The Contracts Early Access flag must be on for the org before Templates appear. Users also need all four org.contracts permissions to author templates; read-only users see the list and editor in a disabled state with a banner.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer on the Contracts beta asks how to create or edit their own agreement template without using the API or Docusign.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org already on the Contracts Early Access flag that wants to use Sessionboard native e-sign rather than Docusign.
internal.staff_path: CRM → Contracts → Templates
internal.gotchas: PDF-mode templates show a notice that field placement is not yet available (CON-201). Archived templates are hidden from the Add Contract picker but can be restored by publishing again. A 409 conflict banner appears if the same template is edited in two browser tabs simultaneously — the user must reload. Variables rail de-duplicates custom properties that appear across multiple events.
internal.talk_track: Go to CRM → Contracts → Templates, create a template, drop in merge variables and signer roles from the rail, add any conditional clauses, then publish. The template shows up immediately in Add Contract → Send with Sessionboard. Every publish creates a new revision you can restore later.

draft.docs_gap: The /speaker-crm/contracts guide should add a section covering the Templates tab: creating and publishing a template, the document editor (variables rail, signer roles, insert blocks, conditional sections), .docx import, Preview as…, revision history, and the read-only state for users without update permission.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's native e-sign lets you send, track, and collect legally binding signatures on agreements without leaving the platform. The template editor gives you full control over the document: pull in contact, session, and event data as merge variables; define who signs and in what order; add conditional clauses that appear only when a field matches; and preview exactly what a specific contact will see before you publish. Once a template is published it is available in the Add Contract flow, and every revision is saved so you can restore an earlier version at any time.

entries.title: Open forms, evaluation plans, portals and tasks as read-only canvases beside Team Lead
entries.summary: In AI Mode, clicking a form, evaluation plan, portal or task record link now opens a read-only canvas beside the docked **Team Lead** panel instead of navigating away to the classic page. Each canvas shows a type label, title, status pill, key facts (questions and settings for forms; rounds, reviewers and workload for plans; tasks, forms, file requests and due dates for portals; applies-to, due date and instructions for tasks), an **Ask about this** button that prefills the composer, and a **Full page** link to the classic view. The **Team Lead** rail also gains **Forms**, **Evaluation plans** and **Portals** sections listing the event's (and org's) records with a prompt to ask Team Lead to build one.

where.path: Team Lead panel → rail → Forms / Evaluation plans / Portals / Tasks, or any record chip in chat

entries.use_case: Organizers who are working through a planning conversation with Team Lead can inspect a form's questions, an evaluation plan's rounds and reviewer workload, a portal's task list, or a task's instructions without losing their place in the chat — then hit **Ask about this** to continue the conversation in context.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to use Team Lead to review or update their evaluation plans, portals, forms or tasks without leaving the AI Mode interface.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer already using AI Mode / Team Lead.
internal.staff_path: Event or Org → Team Lead panel → rail → Forms / Evaluation plans / Portals, or click any record chip in a chat response
internal.gotchas: Portal canvas shows assigned-people count and per-ask deadlines but not per-person completion progress (no existing hook). Task canvas does not indicate which portals include the task. Org-level portal sections are not shown (event only for portals). An org task canvas on an org without the feature ends in an error state after retries.
internal.talk_track: When Team Lead mentions a form, plan, portal or task, click the chip to open it as a canvas right beside the chat. Hit 'Ask about this' to pull that record into your next message, or 'Full page' to go to the classic editor.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the four new canvas types (forms, evaluation plans, portals, tasks) and the new rail sections, including what facts each canvas surfaces and how Ask about this prefills the composer.
draft.why_use_it: The Agent window keeps Team Lead docked beside whatever you are looking at, so you can ask questions and act on answers without switching back and forth between pages. Record canvases let you read the details of a specific form, plan, portal or task right next to the chat, and the **Ask about this** button carries that record into your next message automatically. Use it whenever you want to understand or change a record through conversation rather than hunting through menus.

entries.title: Sign a Sessionboard e-sign contract directly from the portal

entries.title: Email Send Date tags use your date format
entries.summary: **Email Send Date** and the **+7 / +14 / +30 Days** tags now write the date in the event's **Export Date Format** (the organization's for organization-level emails, or when the event follows the organization default) instead of always `YYYY-MM-DD`. where.path: Event settings → Record settings → Dates & IDs → Export Date Format; Organization settings → Details → Export Date Format

entries.use_case: Reply-by dates in emails read the way the rest of your event writes dates, like 06/15/2025 or June 15, 2025.

entries.title: Choose which notifications each event team role receives
entries.summary: Event Team → Permissions has a new **Notifications** tab: for each role, set every automatic notification to **On**, **Off by default** (members can turn it back on in their own preferences) or **Off** (locked for the role). internal.staff_path: Event → Event Team → Permissions → pick a role → Notifications; org defaults at Org → Notifications → Organization policy → Event team role defaults

entries.title: Get told once when every review of a submission is in

entries.title: Share certificates from Print with participants in the Portal

entries.title: Content Galleries: formatted copy on the hub, a per-page choice, and day filters in the event time zone

internal.who_should_get_it: Events collecting video abstracts or files in submission forms, starting with AUA (SB-8063) and anyone who asked to moderate files before evaluators (SB-6669).

entries.title: Awards: a new round saves its scorecard questions
